subject: Initial commit
claim: Repo created with README stub 'toy-physics / Toy Physics Model' and LICENSE; no scientific content.

subject: Add initial toy physics model
claim: Introduces the 'Discrete Alien-Physics Toy Model': an event-network ontology where one shared local edge rule generates stationary-action geodesics that bend inward gravity-like under a proper-time-style action built from an emergent delay field, causal order inferred from positive local delays rather than a global step counter, and measurement as durable-record formation that kills cross-slit interference while single-slit diffraction survives inside each record sector. Pressure tests assert positive-weights-only is too weak for interference, that a Hadamard-style reversible mixer preserves the 2-norm but not 1- or 4-norm totals (favoring the Born-style square), and that sqrt(dt^2-dx^2) is the only tested local scalar invariant under boost-like frame mixing. Declared still-cheating: hand-authored spatial graph geometry, the assumption that histories extremize spent delay dt - sqrt(dt^2-ds^2), hand-chosen rule family and locality preferences, assumed complex amplitudes, and consciousness outside the simulation.

subject: Update README.md
claim: README wording only: drops 'we built in conversation' from the prototype description.

subject: Document model axioms and primitives
claim: States the model axioms (reality is an evolving network of events and influence relations; stable objects are persistent self-maintaining patterns; space is inferred from influence neighborhoods and signal delays; duration is local update count; the arrow of time is the direction of increasing durable-record formation; free systems follow the locally simplest allowed continuation; inertia is undisturbed continuation; gravity is continuation in a distorted continuation structure; measurement is durable records separating previously combinable alternatives; consciousness is in the ontology but not simulated) and the primitives (Event e, Link e->e', delay delta(e,e'), compatibility k(e,e'), History h, weight W(h), record R, stable pattern S, internal update count tau_S(h)). Toy rules add: alternatives without durable records can combine, alternatives tagged by different durable records cannot.

subject: Add robustness sweep
claim: Adds a robustness sweep over rectangular, tapered and skewed graphs crossed with hard or wrapped vertical boundaries and compact or extended local rule families. Result claimed as informative rather than celebratory: under the current search budget the extended rule family is noticeably more robust than the compact one, and skewed geometries often fail to nucleate compact persistent patterns at all. The sweep budget is acknowledged as hand-chosen.

subject: Explain robustness diagnostics
claim: Diagnostics explain the compact/extended gap: the extended family finds compact persistent patterns in more scenarios and produces a larger average boundary-delay span once it does, so its gravity-like distortion is both more available and stronger.

subject: Add failure-mode diagnostics
claim: Failure-mode diagnostics show skewed cases mostly fail by producing empty or fragmented candidate patterns, not by hitting the boundary filter, which points to a pattern-formation weakness rather than a boundary-selection bug.

subject: Improve robustness search
claim: A staged search (stricter point-seed pass followed by a clustered-seed fallback) removes all current 'no pattern' cases in the sweep, shifting the bottleneck from pattern existence to pattern quality. Extended remains more robust than compact and skewed geometries remain the weakest case.
supersedes: 11e85c3e705d6dd3b9d01e6db8c4ce8444863501 — the 'no pattern' failures are removed and the bottleneck is reframed from pattern existence to pattern quality

subject: Guide robustness search by winning rules
claim: A guided quality-rescue pass that prioritizes winner-rule motifs upgrades the sweep to 11 surviving scenarios out of 12, leaving only one mixed skewed case.

subject: Explain skew-wrap compact failure
claim: Focused skew-wrap diagnosis: the reduced compact sweep omits the rescuing motif S[3,4]/B[1,3], and once the full compact family is allowed the same case upgrades to 'survives'. The remaining gap is therefore about reduced sweep coverage and search budget, not a deep split between compact and extended ontologies.
supersedes: 3668c0e8e40f703aaae65d5a727cd9b1b3b1c34a — the last mixed skewed miss is reattributed to sweep coverage rather than ontology
red_flags: Identifies the earlier skew-wrap miss as an artifact of reduced rule-family coverage.

subject: Adopt motif-preserving compact sweep
claim: A motif-preserving reduced compact family survives all six tested scenarios using only four count options {3},{1,3},{2,3},{3,4}, derived from the full-compact hard-topology winners skew-hard -> S[2,3]/B[3] and skew-wrap -> S[3,4]/B[1,3]; the extended family also survives all six. Extended still produces the larger average boundary-delay span while reduced compact keeps a slightly larger average center gap. The earlier skew-wrap miss is now labeled a legacy reduced-family coverage bug rather than a compact-vs-extended ontology split.
supersedes: d6a20c0ea1ecaafffcfae645974cce064e70d8c9 — promotes the diagnosis into an adopted repaired compact family
red_flags: Explicitly labels the earlier result a 'legacy reduced-family coverage bug'.

subject: Ablate minimal compact motifs
claim: Exhaustive minimization inside the repaired compact family {3},{1,3},{2,3},{3,4} shows one motif is still redundant, so the actual surviving compact subset is {1,3},{2,3},{3,4}. One-by-one ablation shows all three remaining motifs are indispensable in the current sweep: removing {1,3} breaks skew-wrap, removing {2,3} breaks taper-wrap, and removing {3,4} causes the broadest collapse.
supersedes: f069cb32805f8ac112f857c9f0e77e762eda2aa9 — the four-option minimal compact set is reduced to three options

subject: Ablate mechanism assumptions
claim: Mechanism ablation: removing the delay field collapses the effect and weakening field relaxation breaks the hardest wrapped skew case, so the field side is genuinely load-bearing. Weak spot admitted: replacing the proper-time-style action with plain coordinate delay weakens the sweep, but a bare link-length action still passes the current robustness metric, so the action principle is not yet uniquely selected.
red_flags: Admits the action principle is not uniquely selected by the current robustness metric.

subject: Add action-response discriminator
claim: With an action-response discriminator added (the benchmark now also requires the distorted geodesic to move relative to the free geodesic), the spent-delay action with relaxed field propagation is the only tested mechanism that both survives and responds.
supersedes: ca3dc25c6216aeadf10ba9b93319675733edce3a — closes most of the admitted 'action not uniquely selected' gap

subject: Sweep retained-weight action family
claim: A broader retained-weight action-family sweep: the low-weight half of the family fails the combined benchmark while only the high-weight end survives, with the strongest wrapped-case response at the full spent-delay point w = 1. The discriminator wording is simultaneously softened from 'only tested mechanism' to 'only named mechanism'.
supersedes: 30f6fc3909cb47f5b1a2f6a0d8b1b4a0f1a2b3c4 — narrows the discriminator claim from 'only tested' to 'only named' mechanism

subject: Broaden retained-weight benchmark
claim: A cross-pack benchmark across larger and mirrored scenario packs still favors the high-retained-update end but does not yet collapse the retained-weight family all the way to a single exact coefficient.

subject: Add proper-time consistency benchmark
claim: A high-end proper-time consistency benchmark over w = 0.75..1.00 that checks every off-center boundary target across all packs finds that w = 1.0 is the only retained weight keeping the action gain larger than the extra coordinate delay in the current grid.
supersedes: d4da9578f96c1a7b0e5a41b7f5c0d29e6b7c8d90 — the retained-weight family is now collapsed to the single point w = 1.0

subject: Rename model to octopus physics
claim: MODEL RENAME: README title changes from 'Discrete Alien-Physics Toy Model' to 'Discrete Octopus-Physics Toy Model' and the ontology is relabeled a compact 'octopus physics' ontology. Also adds critical-weight case machinery (path retained totals, critical-weight case table).
supersedes: e26e40f9633105236fef3976b7b235fcb9432fec — model renamed from alien-physics to octopus-physics

subject: Explain retained-weight branch crossing
claim: Decomposition of the retained-weight crossing: for a fixed distorted path the consistency margin is linear in w with a calculable critical weight w* = 2 * delay_penalty / retained_total, and the hardest observed cases sit just below 1.0.

subject: Clarify README branch-crossing result
claim: In the hardest observed targets the largest critical weights are all in large:skew-wrap-large, clustered around w* ~= 0.953..0.955. The hardest scenario does not stay on one branch across the scan: at w = 0.75..0.90 the active winner is S[2,3]/B[3,4] with source row -1 and a much easier threshold w* ~= 0.794, and the optimum switches near the crossing. The retained-weight benchmark is therefore a piecewise-linear lower envelope of active rule/path branches rather than a single line in w, which is why w = 0.95 still fails while w = 1.0 passes.
supersedes: a54ec6af6b5aff04b08106d2501d17865dfa5165 — adds branch-switching structure and corrects the single-line-in-w reading
red_flags: Corrects a naive single-branch reading of the retained-weight benchmark.

subject: Separate README claims and explain rule switch
claim: README is restructured to separate conceptual motivation from what the script implements, what it demonstrates, and what is still cheating; it states that the retained-update term sqrt(dt^2-dx^2) is motivated by the boost symmetry test while the spent-delay action carries an extra accounting assumption that still has to be justified. A new selection diagnostic explains the rule switch: the fallback branch is structurally stable across the scan but its center gap degrades from 0.241 to 0.013 as w rises, dropping it from 'survives' to 'mixed/fragile'.

subject: Formalize naming and freeze branch comparison
claim: MODEL RENAME: README title becomes 'Discrete Event-Network Toy Model' and 'Octopus physics' is demoted to a lightweight project nickname, with the README's claims explicitly about the event-network toy model itself. A frozen-branch comparison holding the two competing persistent patterns fixed and varying only w finds the same qualitative crossover remains, with the old branch becoming more proper-time-consistent as w rises.
supersedes: 233a5a5bc2ac89949419b053ed72fc2958b4b1f2 — 'octopus physics' demoted from model name to project nickname

subject: Explain center-gap collapse geometry
claim: Geometric diagnostic of the center-gap collapse: on the old branch the source row and comparison paths stay fixed while w rises, but the side routes get cheaper faster than the center route, so the center gap collapses because detours become relatively cheaper.

subject: Test robustness metric and selector steering
claim: Metric choice is shown to be genuinely load-bearing: on the hard case raw action-gap metrics favor the rescue branch throughout while pure geometric-focus gap favors the fallback branch throughout, with a mixed 'stiffness' metric in between. A selector-policy ablation shows an ungated selector would already pick the rescue branch at low high-end weights while the current gated selector keeps the fallback branch until it stops surviving, so the observed switch timing is partly a selector artifact. The robustness criterion (center gap, arrival span, gated fallback-then-rescue selector) is admitted to be hand-chosen.
red_flags: Admits the observed branch-switch timing is partly an artifact of the hand-chosen selector gate.

subject: Switch to always-compare selector baseline
claim: Switching to an always-compare selector baseline changes the picture: the hardest case is now mirror:rect-hard-large and the active winner stays S[3,4]/B[1,3] across w = 0.75..1.00, so the sign change is a single-branch effect rather than a late branch switch. The rescue motif is preferred because it carries a much larger arrival span even though the fallback motif S[2,3]/B[3,4] keeps a slightly larger center gap. Always-compare and the legacy gated selector differ in 20/78 compact benchmark pack-weight cases, concentrated in base:taper-wrap and large:taper-wrap-large.
supersedes: 281b41cb7e323b484d054caa566321d5d9113398 — the gated selector is replaced by an always-compare baseline and the late-branch-switch story is retired
red_flags: Retires the earlier late-branch-switch narrative as a gated-selector artifact.

subject: Add selector-free frontier diagnostics
claim: Adds a selector-free Pareto frontier layer that keeps nondominated motifs alive instead of collapsing to one winner; it is diagnostic-only, with the baseline selector still using the always-compare quality key. On the hardest compact case mirror:rect-hard-large the selected rescue motif S[3,4]/B[1,3] sits on the robustness and mixed frontiers across the scanned retained-weight range while the fallback motif S[2,3]/B[3,4] remains nondominated.

subject: Cache selector-free frontier sweep
claim: The cached frontier pass runs end-to-end across all 156 family-pack-weight cases in the benchmark grid; the baseline-selected motif lies on the robustness, proper-time, geometry and mixed frontiers in 52/156, 22/156 and further per-view counts. Frontier reporting is split into a case-level overview, a motif-frequency aggregate across both families, and a hard-case trace, with S[2,3]/B[3,4] appearing on the mixed frontier in the compact sweep.

subject: Add topology perturbation ensemble
claim: First deterministic topology-perturbation ensemble (two small graph nudges per benchmark graph at w = 1.0, tracking the unperturbed frontier palette): mixed-frontier overlap survives in 26/26 perturbed cases for both compact and extended, while robustness overlap and exact selected-winner retention are markedly weaker. Conclusion claimed: some selector-free motif families look topology-robust while the exact baseline winner is topology-sensitive.

subject: Compare perturbation stability across weights
claim: Cross-weight perturbation comparison from w = 1.0 down to w = 0.95: the perturbed selected winner is stable across the two weights, but the fragile part is the stronger overlap claim back to the unperturbed baseline — the base selected motif remains frontier-alive at both weights in only 19/26 compact and 20/26 extended cases. Scope is admitted narrow, covering only the high-end pair w = 0.95 and w = 1.0.

subject: Add seeded random perturbation ensemble
claim: Seeded-random perturbation ensemble (two random removable/addable node choices per scenario): mixed-frontier overlap survives in 26/26 cases for both families, robustness overlap in 22/26 compact and 21/26 extended, while the exact unperturbed winner is retained in only 7/26 compact. Claimed as the strongest selector-free result so far.

subject: Stream perturbation summaries
claim: Code-only: bounded-memory streaming of perturbation summaries (sorted bounded insert, aggregate row builders); no new scientific claim.

subject: Stream cross-weight summary and widen random ensemble
claim: Widened the seeded-random ensemble to three random variants per scenario: mixed-frontier overlap survives in 38/39 compact and 39/39 extended, robustness overlap in 30/39 for both, and the exact unperturbed winner is retained in only 12/39 compact. Explicitly described as 'a little more honest than the earlier two-variant picture'.
supersedes: 84577ffe502424b1d8295b775891d0498d54b39e — the two-variant counts (26/26, 22/26, 7/26) are replaced by three-variant counts

subject: Add high-end perturbation weight ladder
claim: High-end weight ladder over w = 0.90, 0.95, 1.00: the perturbed selected winner stays the same across the full ladder in 25/26 cases for both families; robustness overlap survives in 16/26 for both, and proper-time and geometry overlap in 12/26 compact and 10/26 extended. Weight-robustness is admitted to remain local to a narrow high-end band near the spent-delay point.

subject: Add limited rediscovery random perturbation pass
claim: A limited-rediscovery random ensemble lets each perturbation reintroduce up to two locally rediscovered motifs instead of forcing the unperturbed frontier palette: all 39/39 random cases now survive in both families and mixed-frontier overlap stays 38/39 compact and 39/39 extended, but robustness overlap drops to 29/39 compact. Interpretation given: earlier random robustness was partly propped up by palette inheritance, while the mixed frontier remains the strongest selector-free object.
supersedes: b1ecdca307271b9d85884c2562dfefb1b8f397a7 — relaxes the palette-inheritance cheat, weakening the stronger overlap claims
red_flags: Admits earlier robustness numbers were partly an artifact of frontier-palette inheritance.

subject: Sweep random rediscovery limits
claim: Rediscovery-limit sweep over 0, 1, 2, 3: one extra rediscovered motif already repairs the last random 'fragile' cases in both families and increasing the limit beyond 1 does not improve selected-rule retention. Compact goes survives 38 -> 39, mixed 38 -> 38, robustness 30 -> 29 from limit 0 to 3; extended goes survives 38 -> 39, mixed 39 -> 39, robustness 30 -> 26. The mixed frontier saturates early while the stronger overlap claims are still partly propped up by palette restriction.

subject: Clarify rediscovery README wording
claim: README wording only: relabels the limited-rediscovery ensemble as a 'first' pass and softens 'up to two extra motifs' to 'a small number of locally rediscovered motifs'.

subject: Add geometry-randomized benchmark ensemble
claim: Geometry-randomized benchmark ensemble jitters the entire column profile of each graph into two deterministic whole-shape variants: compact survives in 25/26 cases and keeps mixed-frontier overlap in 25/26, extended survives 26/26 with mixed overlap 26/26, while exact selected-winner retention drops sharply. Claimed as one of the strongest results in the repo — the mixed frontier stays much more stable than the exact winner even when the whole benchmark shape is deformed.

subject: Add procedural graph generator ensemble
claim: Procedural graph-generator ensemble regenerates each graph from scratch inside the same bounding box using a seeded smooth column-profile rule at rediscovery limit 1: both families still survive in 25/26 cases with mixed-frontier overlap 24/26, exact selected-winner retention drops to 7/26 compact and 6/26 extended, and robustness overlap sits at 18/26. Described as harder and more honest than the pack-local tests, and not perfectly stable once the graph family is regenerated independently.

subject: Add procedural miss diagnostic
claim: Diagnostic of the lone compact procedural survive-miss: it still keeps mixed-frontier overlap and its center_gap is actually larger than its nearby surviving sibling; what collapses is arrival_span. Geometrically it is the one case with a cross-midline, high-variation centerline (center_range 3.5 and center_total_variation 8.0 versus 2.0 and 4.0 in the surviving sibling), pointing to a specific sensitivity rather than generic failure.

subject: Add contour sensitivity sweep
claim: A contour-sensitivity sweep holding the span profile fixed and interpolating only the centerline deformation keeps mixed-frontier overlap intact across the whole sweep; the survives -> mixed transition is driven not by generic contour roughness but specifically by deformations that preserve local focusing while suppressing far-boundary delay spread.
supersedes: 84cd10cdd97e61f3e60f47741dbdfffffde84c19 — turns the single-case clue into a controlled mechanism test

subject: Benchmark alternative focus observables
claim: Benchmark of alternative focus observables (the current box-min rule versus harmonic, geometric and arithmetic combinations): all four preserve the strong cases at 12/12 core survives, 51/51 geometry-randomized survives and 50/50 procedural survives, differing only on threshold misses. box-min leaves the contour miss as mixed and promotes no procedural miss; arithmetic and geometric rescue the contour miss but also promote the geometry miss; harmonic is the most conservative smoother, making it the strongest tested candidate for a combined focusing observable.

subject: Add harmonic frontier ablation diagnostic
claim: Running the harmonic observable through the existing selector/frontier machinery (relabeling only, candidate pool held fixed) changes the selected winner in 105/156 cases while keeping the harmonic-selected rule at survives in 156/156; the baseline-selected rule survives under harmonic in 154/156. Under harmonic the selected rule lands on the robustness and mixed frontiers in 78/78 cases for both families, while the old baseline motif remains on the harmonic mixed frontier in only 58/78 compact and 56/78 extended. Conclusion: the sharp box-min status rule is materially steering the selector/frontier picture even at fixed candidate set.
red_flags: Shows the status-observable choice is a live cheat steering results at fixed candidate pool.

subject: Add continuous frontier score ablation
claim: Replacing the discrete survives/mixed/fragile rank with the continuous harmonic score as the leading selector/frontier axis changes the selected winner in only 31/156 cases relative to the bucketed harmonic pass and keeps both winners at survives in 156/156, but almost eliminates frontier disagreement: the selected rule sits on all four frontier views in 78/78 cases for both families. Conclusion: the bucketization step, not the observable change, carries much of the frontier disagreement.

subject: Add derived-axis frontier diagnostic
claim: Derives a covariance-based axis set from the harmonic-continuous candidate pool over center_gap, arrival_span, min_margin, geometric_focus_gap and the harmonic focus score, removing the hand-named frontier vocabulary. The leading derived axis loads +0.469, +0.456 and +0.568 on center_gap, arrival_span and focus score and -0.381 and -0.323 on min_margin and geometric_focus_gap. The selected rule stays on the full pc123 frontier in 153/156 cases but only on pc1 in 122/156 and pc12 in 129/156, and the top derived-axis motif in both families is S[2,3]/B[3,4], on the pc123 frontier in 55/78 compact and 52/78 extended.

subject: Add derived frontier basis ablation
claim: Derived-basis ablation varying the metric basis: focus3 = {center_gap, arrival_span, focus_score}, no_margin and action3 all keep the selected rule on the full pc123 frontier in 156/156 cases, and the weakest tested basis no_focus still keeps it in 144/156; every tested basis has nonempty pc123 overlap with the full five-metric basis in all 156/156 cases. Motif ranking remains basis-dependent: the top pc123 motif stays S[2,3]/B[3,4] for 4/5 bases in compact and 3/5 in extended.

subject: Add derived frontier bootstrap stability map
claim: Bootstrap stability map over 28 basis views (16 subset bases = all 3- and 4-metric subsets plus the full five-metric basis, plus 12 seeded random projection bases): the full-basis reference keeps the selected rule on pc123 in 153/156 cases and every sampled basis has nonempty pc123 overlap in all 156/156. S[2,3]/B[3,4] is the most ensemble-stable pc123 motif — compact 28/28 bases, 1744 basis-case frontiers, 19 top-basis wins; extended 28/28 bases, 1619 basis-case frontiers, 20 top-basis wins — but multiple motif-family pairs appear on pc123 in every sampled basis, so the claim is basis-ubiquity rather than uniqueness.

subject: Broaden derived bootstrap with nonlinear bases
claim: Bootstrap broadened to 37 basis views (16 subset + 12 seeded linear-random + 9 mild nonlinear): 35/37 sampled bases keep full case-by-case pc123 overlap with the reference, the weakest being the nonlinear random view softsign:rand01. S[2,3]/B[3,4] remains fully ubiquitous (compact 37/37 bases, 2270 basis-case frontiers, 25 top-basis wins; extended 37/37, 2124, 26) across all 16/16 subset, 12/12 linear-random and 9/9 nonlinear bases, and 17 motif-family pairs appear on pc123 in every sampled basis.
supersedes: bf913e5aa7d96ed2b1ee46a031a5dd84e5ecf6da — the 28-basis ensemble is extended to 37 with nonlinear views

subject: Clarify nonlinear basis ensemble in README
claim: README clarification only: the nonlinear basis family includes three full-transform views (signed_sqrt, signed_log1p, softsign) plus small random projections of each transformed metric space, making the basis generator broader than a few fixed transforms.

subject: Add transform-strength sweep diagnostic
claim: Transform-strength sweep over 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00 across the three transform classes in both direct and projected variants: no direct transformed basis breaks its identity-strength baseline at all; the first projected transform-induced break appears at strength 0.25 for both signed_sqrt and softsign, while signed_log1p breaks later. The weakest transformed view is softsign:s1.00:rand01 at 145/156 overlap and 71/156 selected-on-pc123, yet the dominant motif S[2,3]/B[3,4] remains present in all 45/45 transform-family views in both families. Conclusion: the fragile ingredient is stronger nonlinear distortion combined with projection, not transformation by itself.

subject: Ablate projection generator and dimension
claim: Bootstrapping 8 deterministic projections per nonlinear mode/strength pair keeps S[2,3]/B[3,4] present in all 120/120 projected bases in both families, but the weakest projected cell now appears at signed_log1p strength 0.00, making projection choice itself the first real instability. Comparing raw, row-normalized and orthonormalized projection generators, none cleanly wins: row_norm gives the best averages, raw keeps the best worst-case minima, and orthonormal improves top-basis dominance while worsening the weakest cells. Varying projection dimension over 2, 3, 4, 5 is sharp: dimension 2 is weakest (107/156 minimum overlap, 33/156 minimum selected-on-pc123), dimension 3 much healthier, and dimensions 4 and 5 nearly restore the full reference, so a real part of the instability is compression-driven.
red_flags: Identifies the random projection generator itself as visibly load-bearing on results.

subject: Add 4D orthonormal stability map
claim: Rerunning the selector-free stability map on the 4D orthonormal family: all 60/60 bases keep nonempty pc123 overlap with the full reference in all 156 cases, and selected-on-pc123 ranges from 130/156 to 156/156. S[2,3]/B[3,4] remains the leading selector-free motif in both families and 18 motif-family pairs are fully ubiquitous across all 60 bases; once the projection bottleneck is widened the residual disagreement looks like motif ranking within a robust family rather than wholesale loss of overlap.
supersedes: 142a76ec224f1eeee6c31cb03d213ae68968fbda — the 3D projection default is replaced by 4D orthonormal as the reference family

subject: Add 4D case-core analysis
claim: Case-core intersection on the 4D orthonormal family (intersecting pc123 motifs across all 60 bases per case): the case core is nonempty in 84/156 cases and the currently selected rule lies inside it in 81/156, but 0/156 cases have core == union and the largest case core has size 4. The strongest unavoidable motifs are narrower than the basis-wide winners: in compact S[2,3]/B[3,4] has 21 core hits out of 78 union hits, while in extended the strongest unavoidable motif is S[3,4]/B[1,3] with 9 core hits.
red_flags: Sharpens and weakens the basis-ubiquity story: ubiquitous is not the same as unavoidable.

subject: Map 4D case-core geometry regimes
claim: Mechanism map grouping the 4D orthonormal cases into empty, single-selected, single-other, multi-selected and multi-other core regimes against column-profile geometry: 72 cases have empty cores and are skew-heavy (37/72, with the same 37/72 midline-crossing count) with higher average center-variation 1.03 and span-range 1.47; 74 cases land in single-selected and are mostly rect+taper shapes (52/74) with lower average center-variation 0.59; the multi-selected regime is small at 7 cases and mostly taper-shaped (6/7). Empty cores are therefore concentrated in rougher, skewed, crossing profiles rather than being random failures.

subject: Add fixed-span roughness core sweep
claim: Fixed-span roughness core sweep varying only centerline roughness: the response is not monotone in the interpolation parameter (realized roughness dips mid-sweep and rises again) but is strongly tied to realized centerline roughness. In compact the low-roughness mid-sweep states (center-variation 2.0) give 6/6 weights selected-in-core while rougher states (5.0, 6.0, 8.0) collapse to all-empty cores; in extended low roughness gives 6/6 multi-selected cores, mid-high roughness 5.0 collapses to 6/6 empty cores, and the roughest endpoint 8.0 partially re-enters single-selected at 5/6.

subject: Add centerline mode basis sweep
claim: Centerline mode basis sweep over independent modes tilt, bowl, step and zigzag at fixed span profile: the broad roughness link survives but mode symmetry matters a lot. In compact, tilt stays mostly single-selected through amplitude 1.0 (5/6 selected-in-core) and step recovers to 6/6 at amplitude 1.5, while zigzag is already fully destructive at amplitude 0.5; in extended, bowl at amplitude 1.5 gives 6/6 multi-selected cores while zigzag collapses to 6/6 empty at amplitude 0.5 and re-enters as 6/6 selected-in-core at 1.5. The roughness/core link is therefore not reducible to roughness magnitude alone; the symmetry class of the deformation is part of the mechanism.
supersedes: e4cbaf8f220131ee9a9e72c35db20ca09dcb0db1 — the single-interpolation-path roughness story is generalized and roughness magnitude alone is shown insufficient

subject: Add centerline invariant mechanism test
claim: Centerline invariant test grouping the fixed-span mode sweep by shape signature (smooth-monotone, step-like, curved, oscillatory) plus whether the centerline crosses the midline: at identical roughness the outcomes split sharply by invariant class — compact at center-variation 2.0 gives curved/no-cross 1/6, smooth-monotone/cross 5/6, step-like/cross 3/6 selected-in-core; extended at center-variation 6.0 gives curved/cross 6/6 versus oscillatory/no-cross 0/12. Across the sweep there are 9 roughness groups where identical center-variation splits into different case-core outcomes by invariant class, so monotone-vs-oscillatory and crossing-vs-non-crossing explain the behavior better than roughness alone.

subject: Benchmark predictive geometry feature subsets
claim: Predictive test with tiny decision trees under leave-one-mode-out generalization: in compact roughness-only is best at 0.46 accuracy ahead of mixed 0.44 and invariant-only 0.43; in extended roughness-only and mixed tie at 0.59 ahead of invariant-only 0.51 — so the invariant bundle is explanatory but not the best predictive compression. An exhaustive search over all raw 1-, 2- and 3-feature subsets finds compact's best subset is turning_points + crosses_midline at 0.56, beating roughness-only, while several extended summaries tie at 0.59. Fold-stability is weak: compact has no repeat fold winner at all, and extended splits 2/4 center_range versus 2/4 center_variation.
supersedes: b99b2808cfa07db7eeefe9a78d248919a63f0013 — the headlined invariant bundle is shown incomplete; smaller raw feature subsets match or beat it
red_flags: Admits the previously headlined invariant bundle is not the best predictive compression.

subject: Test geometry predictors out of family
claim: Out-of-family transfer test (train the geometry predictors on the full mode sweep, then test them unchanged on the roughness sweep and the independently generated procedural family at w = 1.0) reverses part of the in-family story: in compact roughness-only transfers best at mean accuracy 0.77 including perfect accuracy on the roughness family, while the in-family winner turning_points + crosses_midline drops to 0.40; in extended roughness-only and mixed tie at 0.56 while the in-family best center_range falls to 0.50. Some of the extra in-family predictive lift was mode-family-specific.
supersedes: aec981517fe5a11f87d1a12b1001a812e7dee94d — the in-family best feature subsets fail to transfer; roughness-like summaries are the most transfer-stable
red_flags: Out-of-family transfer contradicts the in-family feature-subset winners.

subject: Map Pareto-stable geometry predictors
claim: Selector-free predictor map scoring every raw 1..3 feature subset by both mode-sweep CV and out-of-family transfer, keeping only nondominated subsets: compact's raw fronts hold 7 balanced and 5 transfer subsets that compress to 5 distinct predictor behaviors with roughness-only on both fronts, while extended's 11 balanced and 16 transfer subsets compress to just 2 distinct behaviors (most of the raw frontier count was redundant supersets of the same roughness-style split). The claim is no longer 'this one subset wins' but that roughness-like summaries are structurally stable across transfer.

subject: Ablate predictor depth stability
